notes: Ish by Peter H. Reynolds is about a boy named Ramon who loves to draw until his brother Leon laughs at his work. His sister Marisol saves his crumpled drawings and frames them, helping Ramon see that art can be 'ish' — not perfect, but expressive and good enough. Key vocabulary themes: creating art, emotional reactions (cry, laugh, happy), the vase drawing, and the concept of 'beautiful' imperfection. The words 'crumple' and 'idea' are critical to the story arc. Words 'vase' and 'flower' and 'notebook' are already in existing activity_images which is helpful. The word 'ish' itself is abstract and not easily picturable, so it has been omitted from fringe in favour of more concrete communicative vocabulary.
